open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” in `models`; `canonical_values` “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` only applies it, or does `canonical_values` own the order itself?
options: `models` owns the members and order; `canonical_values` imports and compares them
Split ownership between the two modules
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the members and order, and `canonical_values` only implements highest-class computation from that order.

open_points.subject: randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: “`trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.”
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation, its randomness source, and collision retry for records written by several different modules?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks every random record ID
Each domain module mints its own IDs and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level identity source owns random minting
open_points.default_guess: `store` mints each ID and retries atomically when it collides.

open_points.subject: agent-name uniqueness during configuration reload
open_points.text: M27 says “names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start”; A16 says “Exactly three checks apply to a re-read” and those checks do not include duplicate agent names.
open_points.question: What happens when a hot-reloaded token list contains two different agent tokens with the same `agent_name`?
options: Reject the re-read and enter the invalid-token-list state
Accept it because reload performs exactly the three listed checks
Accept it but define how the two tokens map to one Actor identity
open_points.default_guess: Reject the re-read; agent-name uniqueness remains an installation invariant after reload.

open_points.subject: flow constants in an unproven flow version
open_points.text: M16 says a constant’s `value` is “a StoredValue (M21)”; M21 defines StoredValue as “One validated value”; A05 checks whether the constant “value fits the port” during proof and says “Composition keeps any other flow version whether or not it is proven.”
open_points.question: How is a flow version retained when its constant value fails the proof’s value-fit check, given that the constant must already be a validated StoredValue?
options: Store a separate raw constant representation until or despite proof failure
Treat a non-fitting constant as a malformed composition request and keep no version
Permit StoredValue records whose bytes do not validate against their stored schema
Require validity against the constant’s declared schema before storage, leaving only declared-schema-versus-port mismatch as a proof failure
open_points.default_guess: Validate and store the constant against its own declared schema before composition; only a mismatch between that schema and the target port remains a retained proof failure.

open_points.subject: attempt number used by pre-record spooled files
open_points.text: “`store` alone assigns `attempt_number` ... no caller passes a number”; later, a file “is named by the element’s next ordinal, which the spooling module reads as the count of the element’s NodeExecutions plus one.”
open_points.question: Does `store` compute and return the ordinal when a file is spooled, or do `runs` and `effects` read and compute that ordinal before calling `store`?
options: `store.spool_file` computes and returns the next ordinal
The spooling module computes and passes the ordinal
The store reserves an attempt ordinal before any files are spooled
open_points.default_guess: `store.spool_file` computes and returns the next ordinal, and the later record write verifies that it is still next.
